I just wanted to share after our meeting last month, and before we look at the policy again, I wanted to share some information with you all about our workers' compensation program. So workers' compensation covers all employees, full-time, part-time, coaches, etc., who have an injury that arises out of and in the course of their employment. Not every injury that

occurs in the workplace is a workers' comp injury. LCPS provides a panel of physicians from whom an employee can seek treatment under workers' comp. That's not to say that if an employee needs to seek treatment at an emergency room or urgent care that it will not be covered. However, in those cases where a panel provider is not accessible or it is a non-emergent circumstance, a panel physician must be consulted. For those who see an off-panel provider, an emergency room, an urgent care that's not on the list, any referral or follow-up care has to go through the panel physician. So they can go to the emergency room, they can go to urgent care,

whatever they need to do. But any follow-up care, refer to a specialist, etc., has to go through that panel physician so they will have to choose a panel physician off of the list. LCPS has a third-party administrator, PMA Companies, who manages the care and administration of our workers comp claims. PMA maintains a list of qualified specialists for any employee who is referred to a specialist for follow-up care. Next slide. There are three types of claims. There's lost time, there's medical only, and there's record only. Employees who have an approved workplace injury

are eligible for lifetime medical treatment for that injury. It doesn't matter if it's medical only or if they had actually missed time for it. If the injury, 10 years later, they have an issue related to the injury, it's still going to be covered under workers' compensation.

Employees who missed time due to an improved workers' comp injury receive 66 and two-thirds of their pay, and that's Code of Virginia. This is paid directly to the employee, and it is non-taxable, so it works out pretty close to their regular pay. In Virginia, there is a maximum 10-year period for that lost time payment.

The majority of injuries that occur at LCPS do not require an employee to miss time from work. Next slide. So in order to compare apples to apples, we reviewed workers' compensation claims from July 1 to April 30 for FY19, FY22, and FY23.

We did not utilize 20 or 21 due to the pandemic. Those numbers are not indicative. So in comparing these three years, there's a total difference of 30 claims between the highest number to the lowest number.

And when we looked further, we see that the biggest difference was in the FY22 lost time claims. After we reviewed the claims and spoke with our third-party administrator, it appears that a lot of the lost time was related to slips and falls or struck by claims, which are our highest claims overall.

In FY23, having been back in the classroom for a year, back in the buildings for a year, our claims have, lost time claims have decreased as everybody adjusted to making sure that when you walk by the water fountain, you don't walk through the water or, you know, if the kids are out playing basketball that you don't stand on the court, for example. Our top three categories for claims are struck or injured by, slips and falls, and strains. We work with special education, support services to minimize those injuries as much as possible providing

safety equipment where identified including special non-slip shoes to be used when waxing floors cleats for winter safety or non-slip shoes for custodial staff next slide so the next two slides were provided by PMA companies they compared seven public educational institutions in their book of business to each other they're all Virginia school systems as a percent of payroll on workers comp claims lcps is line f and if you look at the chart it's hard to see from here

Next slide. HRTD's leave and disability programs team works with employees and across departments to ensure that we are providing the best possible use of resources to support our employees and allow them to perform their jobs safely.

In addition, when a significant injury occurs, we work in collaboration with the support services OSHA team to ensure that a full investigation is done and and make changes if needed for employee safety.
